**Lore:** The king of the forest. Taller than a man at the shoulder, it was hunted in deep snow when it could not run.

**The tell:** it lowers its head and paws the ground. **Drops:** a great deal of meat, and antler.

IN THE GAME: Strengths: great reach with its antlers, and it does not scare. Weaknesses: cannot turn quickly in trees; keep
a trunk between you.

entries.title: Adder
entries.decided: in the game's BESTIARY (Game Developer); Robin has not reviewed the text
entries.summary: The only venomous snake of the North. Basks on warm stones, strikes when stepped on.
entries.body:
**Folk name:** Huggorm. **Where:** sunny rocks and the edges of the beach.

**Lore:** The only venomous snake of the North. It basks on warm stones and strikes only when stepped on or cornered.

**The tell:** it coils and lifts its head. **Drops:** nothing worth keeping.

IN THE GAME: Snake blood is a cost of the claim stone. Strengths: hard to see in the grass; its bite burns. Weaknesses: short
reach and a soft body.

ROBIN DECIDED: On 2026-10-22 (through Clive, GD), **no adders on the starter island.** They live on the big island and beyond:
"maybe the adders shouldnt be on the starter island. You have no use for the blood yet." Snake blood is for the claim stone,
which is chapter 2.

PROPOSED: Folk on the big island say every adder is a tiny piece of the Serpent, and that is why its blood goes into the
claim stone's red: it binds the stone to the world's edge. Nobody can say where they heard it. (Moved from the starter
island's folk, 2026-10-22.)

entries.title: The burnt steading
entries.decided: Robin's idea (2026-10-05): a broken village on the home island where the first friendly person is met and the first legendary Viking is heard of. Robin, 2026-10-16: the hero comes to it while the survivor, Arnor, is there scavenging and fixing what he can; he was left alive to tell the story.
entries.summary: The steading on the starter island that Ormr Midgardbane burned two winters ago. A burnt hall, a hut still whole, a plank house by the well, a palisade with gaps, and Arnor in the ruin, mending what he can.
entries.tags: chapter 1, the first home, ruins, the survivor
entries.body:
A burnt hall with its walls knocked in. A wattle hut still whole. A plank house by the well missing five walls and its roof,
which becomes the hero's first home when he mends it. A palisade with gaps. Crates to break. And [[person.arnor|Arnor]],
the smith, in the ruin when the hero comes over the rise, scavenging and fixing what he can (Robin, 2026-10-16). The dead
under the turf behind the hall.

PROPOSED: **Whose it was.** It was [[person.thorgunna|Thorgunna]]'s steading, and the folk of the big island still call it
that. Behind the hall: the graves, each with a small marker, and Thorgunna's under the biggest stone, with Arnor's crooked
runes. By the well, toppled: the steading's old claim stone (the game already has one; raising it is how the hero makes the
place his). In the smithy: Arnor's broken forge, the anvil split, which he has never mended, because he wants it seen.

PROPOSED: **Arnor's mending.** Small things show he has been at work for two winters: a door rehung on new hinges in a house
with no roof, a new bucket on the well, a shutter that closes. He fixes what he can, not what is needed.

IN THE GAME: Today the game calls it "Hildir's steading", Brokk stands by the well, and Ragnar's crew burnt it. The names
change with Robin's decision of 2026-10-16.

IN THE GAME: Built by the Game Developer from lore handoff 1 (commit 03613fa, 2026-10-16): the map label is "The burnt steading". The first claim stone raised there names the place "Thorgunnastead" (the Game Developer's word, marked LORE? in the code).

PROPOSED: Name the claimed place **Thorgunnastad**, after her and the old ending *-stad*, "place". It keeps her name on the land, which is the point of a claim stone, and sounds like the rest of Skargard's place names.

entries.title: The troll's cave
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-06 (copper, the troll and the cave, the arm ring from the dead Viking at the back) and 2026-10-16 (Hårungen)
entries.summary: A cave in the big island's mountain: a daylight tunnel, a pool, a chasm, copper veins, the troll's lair, and behind it, the dead Viking with the bronze ring.
entries.tags: chapter 2, the troll, copper, the arm ring
entries.game: src/cave.js; the troll's cave in templates/game.html
entries.body:
One way through from a tunnel of daylight: a hall, a hollow under a hole in the roof, a still pool, a cavern split by a chasm,
a gallery of copper veins, the [[being.bergtroll|troll]]'s lair, and behind it the dead Viking with the
[[thing.bronze-ring|bronze ring]]. [[being.harungen|Hårungen]] bonk at the ore with their bones.

The dead man is [[person.hogni|Hogni]], who went into the hill forty winters ago with his brother
[[person.aslak|Aslak]] and did not come out. Scratched low on the rock beside him, as if by a man sitting down: *"Hogni.
Tell Aslak to run faster."* Aslak tells the story of that day at the village fire on the big island, so the hero has heard
of the cave, the little ones and their father before he ever goes in (Robin's connection, 2026-10-16).

entries.title: Kvennaey, the Women's Isle
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (first sight is only draugr and abandoned ships; past them, lush green places with large acres and plentiful life; the way in is the season when men are invited, opened up by a quest, meeting one of the women on another island who helps put a marker on where to go; the season's end warns the player through lore)
entries.summary: The island of Skuld's Daughters in the far west. A beach of wrecks and drowned men, and behind it the most beautiful island in Skargard. Men may land only in the invited season, and only if asked.
entries.tags: Kvennaey, the drowned, the invited season, a quest
entries.body:
**First sight** (Robin). From the sea there is nothing but draugr and abandoned ships. The beach is lined with wrecks: good ships,
rotting, their stems still carved, every one of them a man who came uninvited. The daughters call the beach **Nóatún**, "the
Place of Ships", after Njörd's own hall on the shore. The drowned stand in the shallows among the wrecks.

**Past the beach** (Robin). Lush, green and beautiful: wide fields of barley and flax, orchards, hay meadows, beehives, flocks on
every slope, a hall with smoke and singing over it, and women at work everywhere. Njörd gives fertility and wealth as well as the
sea's protection (norse-mythology.org, *Njord*), and Kvennaey has all three. The most beautiful island in Skargard sits behind
the most dreadful beach, and the contrast is the point.

**The way in** (Robin). Only in the season when men are invited, and the way is opened by a quest: on another island the hero
meets one of the daughters, and she helps put a marker on his chart.

PROPOSED: **How the invitation works.**
- **The invited season is summer**, generally (Robin, 2026-10-17: it depends on how the game handles the seasons).
- **The choosing.** Every spring the daughters sail to the markets of the west to choose that summer's guests. The hero meets
  [[person.geirhild|Geirhild Skuldardottir]] at one of them. She watches him, asks his name and what he has done, and if she
  likes the answer she gives him a **braid** (the island's token) and marks Kvennaey on his chart. That is the quest's marker,
  and the only way the island appears on the map.
- **The rule of the braid.** A man who carries the braid may land in summer, and the drowned stay down. Without it, or out of
  season, they rise.

PROPOSED: **The season's end, warned in the island's own way** (Robin: the season's end must warn the player through lore; the warnings themselves are still to come back to).
1. **The drowned come closer.** As summer runs out, they stand a step higher up the beach at every dusk. The player can see the
   end coming from the hall.
2. **The parting gift.** In the last days the daughters give the guest his parting gift. The *Hávamál* says gifts are given at
   parting, and on Kvennaey every guest learns that a gift means *go*.
3. **One word, plainly.** Geirhild, or any daughter he has befriended, says it once: *"The winter nights are close. Be on your
   ship before dark."*

If the player turns the season while still ashore, he is walked into the sea at dusk, and the sea gives him back (it always has,
with him), but the island's trust is gone. What that costs in play is the game's to decide.

IN THE GAME: For the Game Developer to shape, from what Robin decided: men land only in the invited season, with the braid,
and the drowned rise against them otherwise; [[person.ari|Ari]] can be hired as a hirdman; and the rune
[[thing.rune-brimgrid|Brimgr]] keeps the draugr off. The rest (women of the hird going ashore, shieldmaidens, the island's
arrows) are the lore's hints, not rules.

entries.title: Brimgr
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (a rune for the hero's arm ring that makes the draugr not attack him unless attacked; its name is Brimgr). How it is learnt is still to come.
entries.summary: A rune the drowned respect. Draugr leave the one who carries it alone, unless he strikes first.
entries.tags: runes, the arm ring, draugr, Kvennaey
entries.body:
**Robin's rune.** Cut into the hero's arm ring, it keeps the draugr from attacking him unless he attacks them. Its name is
**Brimgr** (Robin, 2026-10-17). How it is learnt is still to come.

PROPOSED: **What folk say of it.** *Brim* is the old word for the sea where it breaks on the shore. The western fishermen say the
drowned know their own, and a man who carries Brimgr has the sea's mark on him, so the dead of the sea let him pass as one of
theirs.

PROPOSED: **The daughters' tale.** On Kvennaey they say the first Skuld cut it, the only rune she ever cut, into a ring for the
one man she ever loved, so that he could walk out past the drowned and live. He did. Nobody knows where he went, and the queens
of Kvennaey have never cut it for anyone since.

entries.title: Tyrsholm
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-20 (the name; the town heavily armed and guarded behind massive stone walls; the arena next to the town; a statue of Týr in stone; the townsfolk cannot leave, and a raft is swallowed by the sea)
entries.summary: Týr's holm: a walled town of stone on its own island, the arena beside it, and a stone Týr over both. The people who live there cannot leave.
entries.body:
**The name** (Robin chose it, 2026-10-20). A holm is a small island, and duels were fought on one. In the duel, a man who stepped
out of the marked ground with both feet had fled. In Tyrsholm the whole island is the duelling ground, and nobody steps off it.

**The town** (Robin). It is heavily armed and guarded, behind massive stone walls. The arena is next to the town, and a statue of
[[god.tyr|Týr]] in stone stands over it. Only [[family.shield-wall|the Shield-wall]] are fed. The townsfolk cannot leave: they
are too poor for a ship, and the sea round Tyrsholm swallows a raft.

PROPOSED: **The stone Týr** has one hand, as Snorri tells it. His right arm ends at the wrist, and every fighter touches the stump
on his way in. **The arena** is marked out with hazel posts, as a duelling ground was, and folk call it the Hazel-field. The
highborn fight there with three shields, and the thrall across from them has one, and a blunt edge.

IN THE GAME: The generator places Tyrsholm. Robin will come back to how the hero fights in its arena (2026-10-20).

entries.title: Skuggaby
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-21 (the town of the Trollvinir, built around the troll cave to keep the sun off, so that trolls can walk in it by day; the name; in the north)
entries.summary: "Shade-town": the Trollvinir's town in the north, built round a troll cave, with every lane roofed over so that its trolls can walk in it by day.
entries.body:
**The town** (Robin, 2026-10-21). It is built round the troll cave, and built to keep the sun off. The lanes are roofed and the
houses lean together, so that trolls can walk in the town by day without turning to stone.

PROPOSED: Under the roofs it is always dusk, and the lanterns burn at noon. The cave mouth opens into the middle of the town, and
the biggest hall is built against it, so that the feast-table runs from the hearth into the mountain. From the fjord the
town looks like a hill with smoke coming out of it.

IN THE GAME: The generator places it in the north. Robin's troll lore holds here as everywhere: a troll caught in daylight
turns to stone ([[being.bergtroll]]).

entries.title: The claim stone
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-06 (stone and berries for the red of the runes; several stones, each after the first needs a hirdman as its keeper)
entries.summary: A raised stone with your mark cut and reddened in it. It makes a place yours, and the hird gathers at it.
entries.body:
A *bautasteinn*, a raised stone, as Vikings did raise to claim and to remember. Stone, and berries for the red of the runes,
and snake blood (as built). Every stone after the first needs a hirdman to stay as its keeper.

PROPOSED: The words cut in a claim stone follow the old formula: *"[The hero's byname] raised this stone. This land is his,
and his men's."* Raising the burnt steading's own toppled stone is how the hero makes Thorgunna's land his. The berries and
the blood are for the [[being.landvaettir|land-spirits]].

entries.title: Runestones
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-06 (runestones give the odd runes; reading one is a rite)
entries.summary: Stones raised for the dead, cut with who raised them, for whom, and one deed. Some of them hold a rune that changes how a thing is done.
entries.body:
Real runestones follow one formula: *who raised the stone, for whom, and what they did*. "Tóla raised this stone for her son
Harald, Ingvar's brother. They went bravely far for gold, and in the east fed the eagle." (The Gripsholm stone.) Most are
raised by women for husbands and sons who went away and did not come back.

PROPOSED: Every runestone in the game carries one such line, generated from the names of the place and its dead, and some
carry a rune (the odd ones, Robin's). The text of a stone is the first lore a player reads, so it should be beautiful, short,
and about a person.

entries.title: Churches
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-07 (churches with friendly priests who cannot defend themselves: lucky strikes, though an army may turn up)
entries.summary: The White Christ's houses in the south: cut stone, a bell, silver on the altar, and a priest who does not fight.
entries.tags: the south, raids, the White Christ
entries.game: Village ARCH church and town; ROLES.priest
entries.body:
Cut stone, a slate roof, a bell tower at the side, silver on the altar and a priest who will not lift a hand. Robin's "lucky
strikes, though an army may turn up".

SAID: "Peace be upon this house, stranger." — a priest
SAID: "The silver on the altar is God's, not mine. He will know who took it." — a priest

PROPOSED: Folk belief says the [[being.vasen|väsen]] cannot bear church bells, so the country round a church has fewer of
them, and the folk there are less careful.

entries.title: The arm ring
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-06 (docs/arm-ring.md): runes are knowledge cut into the ring and reddened with blood; the metal is the rank (bronze, silver, twisted silver, gold, and a fifth). Robin, 2026-10-19: the fifth is not to be called "dragon".
entries.summary: Every free person wears one; the metal is the rank. Runes cut into it and reddened with the wearer's blood have power. Oaths are sworn on it.
entries.body:
Every Viking wore arm rings, jarls gave them to their men, oaths were sworn on them, and in Egil's saga runes cut and reddened
with blood had power (Robin's system, which the game never explains). **The metal is the rank: bronze, silver, twisted
silver, gold, and a fifth whose name is still to come** (Robin, 2026-10-19: the fifth ring is not to be called "dragon": "We shouldnt use dragon, i dont think it makes sense viking-wise. We need more of a viking theme."). Every figure in the world wears its ring on the arm and is named by it in speech ("Ormr of the gold
ring").

| Ring | Coils | Where it comes from (the game) | Who wears it (the lore, proposed) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bronze | 2 | the dead Viking behind the troll's lair | free farmers, steading heads, Arnor, Aslak and Hogni's father |
| Silver | 3 | a jarl or hoard of the second biome | jarls of the new houses, captains, Önund |
| Twisted silver | 4 | later biomes | jarls of the old houses, sea-queens, the Haleygs |
| Gold | 6 | the hall in the south | sea-kings and the old royal blood: Ormr, the Skjoldings, the Scale-keepers |
| The fifth (name to come) | 8 | the thing the legends are about | Odin, once. See [[thing.odins-ring]] |

PROPOSED: **The words of the rite.** Oaths are sworn *by Ullr's ring* (see [[god.ullr]]). When a rune is cut and reddened at the
carver's bench, the old words would be: *"I cut, I redden, I bind."* The game says none of it out loud.

entries.title: The bronze ring
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (Aslak's lines approved: the ring was the brothers' father's, worn by Hogni into the troll's hill). In the game since step 5 of docs/arm-ring.md.
entries.summary: The first ring of the game, taken from a dead man at the back of the troll's cave. Two coils, hand and foot.
entries.tags: the arm ring, the troll's cave, Aslak and Hogni
entries.body:
Two coils: the hand and the foot. The hero takes it from the dead Viking at the very back of the troll's cave, behind the
lair. The smith's taught rune comes after it.

It was [[person.hogni|Hogni]]'s, and before him his father's: a plain old bronze cuff, worn thin on the inside,
which Hogni wore into the troll's hill forty winters ago. His brother [[person.aslak|Aslak]], on the big island, knows it at
once. He will not take it back: *"Keep it. He'd want it to see daylight."* So the hero's first ring is a gift, given twice:
once by the dead, once by the living.

entries.title: Odin's ring
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (the arm rings are crafted or inherited; the most powerful one is legendary and forged by a god: "Forged by Odin himself"). Its name and where it is now are proposed.
entries.summary: The fifth and last ring. Odin forged one ring with his own hands, from the gold of the world's first winter, and cut every rune into it. It is the ring the legends are about.
entries.tags: the fifth ring, Odin, runes, legends
entries.body:
**Robin's ring (2026-10-16):** the most powerful ring is legendary, and was forged by Odin himself. Odin forged it with his own
hands from the gold of the world's first winter, and cut every rune into it. It is the ring the legends are about.

PROPOSED: **The Rune-Ring.** Skalds call it *Rúnbaugr*, the Rune-Ring. Odin hung nine nights on the windy tree to win the
runes, and when he came down he wanted somewhere to keep them. So he forged a ring and cut every rune into it, and reddened
them with his own blood. **Every rune cut into an arm ring since, at every carver's bench in Skargard, is a copy of that
first cutting**, which is why it is done with blood, and why folk say Odin watches. The ring has eight coils and two of every
side: the hand, the foot, the eye and the heart.

PROPOSED: **Where it is now: the legends disagree.**

- It was never in Midgard. Odin wears it, and every one-eyed stranger at a fire has it under his sleeve.
- Odin lent it, with his luck, to the first king of Skargard, and it passed from king to king until [[person.hrolf|King Hrólf]]
  took it west and lost it. (This is the old kings' story; it is why the high seat stands empty. See [[world.high-seat]].)
- Odin gives it, for a while, to the one he means to take to Valhalla. Whoever wears it wins every fight until the last one.
- It lies in the deepest mound in the north, on the arm of a draugr who will not give it up.

The game never says which is true. Each is found where it is told. A player who wears Odin's ring at last can decide which
story he has become.

OPEN: **The fifth ring's name.** Robin, 2026-10-19: the fifth ring is not to be called "dragon": "We shouldnt use dragon, i dont think it makes sense viking-wise. We need more of a viking theme." Proposed, Viking-themed: *rune-gold* (gold with every rune cut in it, as Odin's own
was), *red gold* (the poets' word for the finest gold, Fáfnir's and the Rhine's), *Freyja's tears* (gold, in the skalds'
kennings: Freyja wept red gold), or the rank named for its maker. Draupnir stays a ring of its own ([[thing.draupnir]]): the
dwarves made it, and Robin chose a ring Odin forged himself.

entries.title: Arnor, meeting him
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: Robin's start: the hero comes on Arnor in the ruin, scavenging and fixing what he can. Arnor tells it, because that is what he was left for.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: brokkState meet: the first time E is pressed at the survivor
lines: You came from the sea with less than I have. I didn't think that could be done.
Arnor. I was the smith here. Two winters back Ormr Midgardbane came up the sound and left us this.
He always leaves one. Somebody has to tell it, he said. So here I am, telling it.
The plank house by the well still has its bones. Put walls on it before the dark, if you mean to stay.
entries.body: Arnor never asks who the hero is. He has noticed there is no ring, no kin and no answer, and he lets it be.

entries.title: Arnor, the home has no walls or roof
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: The game's own line first, then two more, so it does not repeat.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: brokkState wait; baseComfort().n is 0
lines: Walls and a roof first. The nights here are not kind.
Four walls and a roof. Everything else is only weather.
I've mended three roofs here since. Nobody to sleep under them. Change that.

entries.title: Arnor, the home has no hearth
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: A smith on fire.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: brokkState wait; the home has a roof but no hearth
lines: A fire in it. A roof without a fire is a cave.
Cold iron takes no shape. Cold men neither. Give it a hearth.
He broke my forge. He didn't think to break the hearthstones. Use them.
entries.body:
TRUE IN PLAY: Since 2026-10-16 (Robin, through the Game Developer) a fire cannot be built indoors on the starter island. A
campfire or hearth burns outside and counts as the house's hearth when it is near the house; a fireplace goes inside only
later. "A fire in it" no longer fits what the player can do there. The line still plays as it is.

PROPOSED: Reworded for Robin to approve: "A fire by the door. A roof with no fire near it is a cave." | "Cold iron takes no
shape. Cold men neither. Build a fire by the wall." | "He broke my forge. He didn't think to break the hearthstones. Carry
them out by the door."

entries.title: Arnor, the home has no bench
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: A smith on benches.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: brokkState wait; the home has a hearth but no workbench
lines: A bench to work at. Hands alone make poor tools.
At a bench I can make anything. Without one I'm a man with a hammer.
Somewhere to sit and mend things. A house where nothing is mended falls down.

entries.title: Arnor, the home has nothing on the floor
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: The last thing a home needs.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: brokkState wait; the home lacks only a rug
lines: Something on the floor. A house is not a home until it is warm underfoot.
Bare boards. Thorgunna would have laughed you out of the hall.
Put a hide down. Cold feet make a man stupid, and you've no wits to spare.

entries.title: Arnor, teaching the raft
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: The home is a home; Arnor teaches the raft and points east, after the sails.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: brokkState teach: Comfort 4 reached
lines: That is a home. Good. Sit a while. First one I've seen here in two winters.
Logs, and rope. Three logs lashed together will carry a man across the sound.
A bench on the sand, by the water. Then east, past the big island. That is where his sails went.

entries.title: Arnor, after the raft is taught
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: Said every time after, so Arnor is not a signpost.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: brokkState taught
lines: The bench on the sand. Lay the logs, and mind the sea.
Tell them on the big island you met Arnor. They'll know the rest. Everyone does.
I'll be here. Somebody has to keep the graves.

entries.title: Arnor, at the graves
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: A new situation: the hero stands among the graves behind the hall while Arnor is near. Said once.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: new: the hero stands among the graves behind the hall for a few seconds, once
lines: Thorgunna, who would not pay. Her two boys beside her. Grímhild, who kept the bees. Thorkel the boatwright.
I cut her runes myself. They're crooked. She'd have laughed at them.
You see? Somebody stands here, and I tell it. Every time. He knew I would.
entries.body: IN THE GAME: Built by the Game Developer from lore handoff 1 (commit 03613fa, 2026-10-16): five stone slabs behind the burnt hall. When the hero stands among them for 2.5 seconds after Arnor's story, Arnor walks over and says the three lines, once.

entries.title: Arnor, at the shore as the hero leaves
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: A new situation from the game's start-loop.md: the survivor walks to the shore and stands there as you paddle out.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: new: the raft first launched from the starter island
lines: Go on, then. And if you hear his story told somewhere, tell them how it ends here.
East. Come back with somebody. This place could use a second voice.
entries.body: IN THE GAME: Built by the Game Developer from lore handoff 1 (commit 03613fa, 2026-10-16): when the first raft is launched, Arnor waits at the shore by the bench and says one line as the hero boards; he goes home when the raft is far away.

entries.title: Arnor, teaching the riposte
entries.decided: in the game since 2026-10-16 (the Game Developer's words, marked LORE? in the code; Robin has not reviewed them)
entries.summary: Arnor's line when he teaches the riposte rune, once the hero wears a ring.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: the first talk with Arnor after a ring is worn (the taught rune)
lines: A ring on your arm, I see. Then take this from me: meet the blow on your shield, and strike while they are still swinging.
entries.body:
PROPOSED: In Arnor's own voice, a smith's: "A ring on your arm. Then you're worth a trick. Take his blow on the shield, and
answer before his arm comes back." (A shade shorter, and a smith teaches by showing, not by naming the rule.)

entries.title: Arnor, joining the hird
entries.decided: in the game since 2026-10-16 (the Game Developer's words, marked LORE? in the code; Robin has not reviewed them)
entries.summary: Arnor's line when the first claim stone is raised and he becomes the first hirdman.
entries.speaker: person.arnor
entries.when: the first claim stone raised on the starter island; Arnor joins
lines: A stone stands again at Thorgunna's. Then I am yours, and this bench is mine.
entries.body: PROPOSED: Keep it as it is. It is in Arnor's voice, short, and it ties the stone to Thorgunna. Recommended for canon.

entries.title: Old Aslak, at the village fire
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: Robin's connection (2026-10-16): an old man in the big island's village who went into the troll's hill with his brother long ago, and tells stories of the troll. His story is the player's guidance, in his own voice.
entries.speaker: person.aslak
entries.when: E at Old Aslak, before the ring is found; said in order over several talks
lines: My brother and I went into the troll's hill when we were young and stupid. I came out.
Little ones in there, all hair and nose. They bonk the stone with bones. Leave them be.
We didn't. One cried, and the father came. I ran for the light. Hogni ran the other way.
He had our father's ring on. It's in there still, past the big one's bed, if the troll left him an arm.

entries.title: Old Aslak, when the hero has the ring
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: A new situation: the first talk with Aslak after the bronze ring is taken from the cave.
entries.speaker: person.aslak
entries.when: new: the first talk with Aslak while the hero has the bronze ring
lines: That's his. … That's our father's ring.
Keep it. He'd want it to see daylight.
He could whistle through his fingers louder than any boy on the island. I'd forgotten that.

entries.title: The folk on Ormr and the sea
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-16 (approved: "Yes, send them")
entries.summary: New pairs for villagers anywhere, carrying Robin's lore of Ormr Midgardbane: the Serpent fears him, no storm touches him, he can call the snake up.
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: E at a villager at peace; one pair per villager
lines: Ormr Midgardbane. Say it quietly. They say the sea listens to him.
The storm that sank my cousin went round his ship like water round a stone.
They say the Serpent fears him. I say the Serpent has more sense than we do.
Pay him. Everybody pays him. The ones who didn't are a story now.
Every place he burns, he leaves one alive. To tell it.
So we'd know what we're paying for.

entries.title: The hamlet's folk, talking
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, FOLK_LINES, 2026-10-05 onward)
entries.summary: The nine pairs the big island's villagers say on E. Each villager has one pair.
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: E at a villager of the hamlet, at peace
lines: Fair winds brought you, or foul?
The well is sweet here. Drink if you like.
Ormr's men came by last winter. We paid them in wool and they left.
Pay, and they leave. Fight, and they burn.
My brother went east with the traders. Rivers all the way, he said.
East is trade. West is nothing but sea.
Colder north of here than you would think.
Keep a fire. Keep a roof. The rest comes.
You will find no work here, but no trouble either.
We mind our own.
The hall in the south has silver on its walls, they say. And a hundred spears round it.
Churches have less spears.
Wolves took two sheep last moon.
They come at night, from the dark wood.
You built that raft yourself? It floats, so it is a boat.
A keel next. Then you can go somewhere.
There is a troll in the hill cave. We leave it be and it leaves us be.
Do not mine there at night.
entries.body:
The game gives each villager a pair (lines 1–2, 3–4 and so on).

ROBIN DECIDED: On 2026-10-16, the raider is Ormr Midgardbane. The game says "Ormr's men" since commit 03613fa.

entries.title: Villagers by their calling
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, ROLES in src/village.js)
entries.summary: What a villager says by their work: fisherman, priest, guard, merchant, farmer, fisher, smith, weaver, elder, child, thrall.
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: E at a villager of a generated village, by their calling
lines: (fisherman) Sit, sit. The sea has been feeding me for sixty years and it has not run dry yet.
(priest) Peace be upon this house, stranger.
(priest) The silver on the altar is God's, not mine. He will know who took it.
(guard) Keep your blade sheathed inside the walls.
(guard) The jarl sees everything from his hall.
(merchant) Wool, salt, iron. What have you got?
(merchant) Silver by weight, friend. We take no promises.
(farmer) The barley came in well this year.
(farmer) Mind the goat: she butts.
(fisher) The herring run at dawn, out past the skerry.
(fisher) That boat has crossed worse water than this.
(smith) Copper is soft. Bring me bog iron and I will show you steel.
(smith) My bench is yours if you leave it as you found it.
(weaver) Wool from our own sheep. Feel it.
(weaver) The loom took a winter to build.
(elder) Ormr's men came once. They will come again.
(elder) My father raised the stone by the gate.
(child) Are you a Viking?
(child) I found a bird's nest with four eggs!
(thrall) ...
(thrall) I was taken from the south. This is home now.
entries.body:
The fisherman's other three lines teach his dishes and are recorded in [[person.fisherman]]. The calling in brackets is the
key; the game has them as lists by calling.

ROBIN DECIDED: On 2026-10-16, the raider is Ormr Midgardbane. The elder says "Ormr's men" since commit 03613fa.

entries.title: The folk, after a blade is drawn
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, WARY_LINES)
entries.summary: A place made uneasy by a drawn blade.
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: the place's unease level is low (a blade drawn, nothing taken)
lines: Keep that blade where it is.
You frightened the children.
We want no trouble here.

entries.title: The folk, after a raid
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, RAIDED_LINES)
entries.summary: A place the hero has raided.
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: the place has been raided by the hero
lines: You again. Take what you want and go.
We have nothing left. You saw to that.
The jarl will hear of this. Everyone will.

entries.title: The folk, cowering during a raid
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, COWER_LINES)

entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: a raid is on and the villager is hiding
lines: Take it. Take all of it.
Not the children.
We have nothing. Nothing.
Gods, not us.
Leave us be.

entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer, HOMELESS_LINES)
entries.summary: A villager whose house has burned.
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: the villager's house is burnt
lines: It is gone. All of it.
Where are we to sleep now?
My father built that house.

lines: You killed {dead}.
{dead} never lifted a hand to you.
{count} of us. {count}.
There is blood on you. Go.
entries.body: The game says the second line when one is dead and the third when more are.

entries.title: A town's guard at the gate
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer)
entries.summary: A walled town lets in only the unarmed and alone.
entries.speaker: role.guard
entries.when: the hero comes to a walled town's gate armed or with men
lines: No blades inside the walls. Leave them at your ship.

entries.title: A guard, challenging a drawn blade
entries.decided: in the game (Game Developer)
entries.summary: A man of the place tells the hero to sheathe his weapon.
entries.speaker: role.guard
entries.when: a blade drawn in a place at peace; CHALLENGE_T

entries.title: A freed thrall, joining
entries.decided: in the game since 2026-10-21 (the Game Developer's words, marked LORE? in the code; Robin has not reviewed them)
entries.summary: A thrall of a raided place, cut loose by the hero, joins the hird (Robin, 2026-10-07).
entries.speaker: role.thrall
entries.when: a thrall of a raided place has just been cut loose and joins the hero
lines: I row, I dig, I fight. Yours.
entries.body:
A thrall in Skargard was taken in a raid or born to it, and the hand-quern, grinding corn and salt, was the hardest work there was (the
Viking Answer Lady, *Slavery and Thralldom*). Once loose he is a [[world.leysingi|leysingi]], a freed man.

entries.title: A taken hirdman, bound
entries.decided: in the game since 2026-10-21 (the Game Developer's words, marked LORE? in the code; Robin has not reviewed them)
entries.summary: One of the hero's hirdmen, left behind on a raid, stands bound at the place that took him, until a later raid frees him (Robin, 2026-10-13). Said as the hero comes near.
entries.speaker: role.hirdman
entries.when: a hirdman of the hero's, taken on an earlier raid, stands bound at that place; the hero comes near
lines: They have had me at the quern. Cut me loose.
entries.body: A free man put to the quern was put to thrall's work, which is the shame in the line.

entries.title: A taken hirdman, freed
entries.decided: in the game since 2026-10-21 (the Game Developer's words, marked LORE? in the code; Robin has not reviewed them)
entries.summary: The same man, the moment he is cut loose.
entries.speaker: role.hirdman
entries.when: the bound hirdman has just been cut loose by the hero
lines: I knew you would come.

entries.title: A man who yielded, let go
entries.decided: in the game since 2026-10-21 (the Game Developer's words, marked LORE? in the code; Robin has not reviewed them)
entries.summary: A man of the place who yielded and is let go by the hero (Robin, 2026-10-07).
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: a man of a raided place has yielded, and the hero lets him go
lines: I will not forget this.

entries.decided: in the game since 2026-10-21 (the Game Developer's words, marked LORE? in the code; Robin has not reviewed them)

entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: a raider dropped a heavy chest in the open, and a man of the place picks it up
lines: Ours, that.

entries.title: The cry over a dead man
entries.decided: in the game since 2026-10-21 (the Game Developer's words, marked LORE? in the code; Robin has not reviewed them)
entries.summary: A villager or a man of the place finds one of their own dead, and raises the cry (Robin, 2026-10-07).
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: a man or woman of the place finds one of their own dead
lines: One of ours is dead! To arms!
Murder! Murder!
entries.body: The Game Developer changed "He is dead!" to fit anyone, man or woman (2026-10-21). "Murder! Murder!" is a villager's.

entries.title: Thief!
entries.decided: in the game since 2026-10-21 (the Game Developer's words, marked LORE? in the code; Robin has not reviewed them)
entries.summary: A villager sees the hero take from their chest or eat their feast before their eyes (Robin, 2026-10-07: that is theft).
entries.speaker: role.villager
entries.when: a villager sees the hero take from their chest or eat their feast
lines: Thief!
entries.body:
In the old laws, the secret thief (*þjófnaðr*) was the worst of all: he could be hanged. Taking openly by daylight was robbery,
and counted less shameful. The villager shouts "Thief!" anyway, because it is the worst word there is (the Lexicon of
Medieval Nordic Law, *þjófnaðr*).

entries.title: A gate man who has heard
entries.decided: in the game since 2026-10-21 (the Game Developer's words, marked LORE? in the code; Robin has not reviewed them)
entries.summary: The gate man of a place that has heard of the hero's raids elsewhere: word spreads to the places near (the Game Developer).
entries.speaker: role.guard
entries.when: the hero comes to the gate of a place that has heard of a raid of his; {place} is the raided place
lines: We know what you did at {place}.
entries.body: "Pay, or burn" are the words of [[family.ormsmenn|Ormr's men]]. A raider's name goes ahead of him, the way Ormr's did.

entries.title: The crew, as the hero steps aboard
entries.decided: in the game since 2026-10-21 (the Game Developer's words, marked LORE? in the code; Robin has not reviewed them)
entries.summary: The first man aboard, as the hero steps into the ship.
entries.speaker: role.hirdman
entries.when: the hero steps into a ship with his men aboard
lines: To the oars.
entries.body:
The man at the steering oar is the *stýrimaðr*, the steersman. On a trading ship he was the master. The steering oar hung on
the right side, the steer-board (*stjórnborði*), which is why the right side of a ship is still starboard.

entries.title: A hirdman with no seat
entries.decided: in the game since 2026-10-21 (the Game Developer's words, marked LORE? in the code; Robin has not reviewed them)
entries.summary: A hirdman who cannot board, because every seat is taken.
entries.speaker: role.hirdman
entries.when: the hird boards, and every seat on the ship is taken
lines: No room for me aboard.

entries.title: The lonely brother
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (the first rumours approved: "Sure")
entries.summary: A villager's brother went west to an island of women, and was never heard from again.
entries.heard: villagers anywhere at home and in the west
lines: My brother was a lonely man. He'd heard of an island out west with only women on it, and went to try his luck. Not a word since.
My brother used to tell of a land in the west with no men in it. He was a lonely sort. One spring he went to see for himself.
entries.body: Robin's own example (2026-10-17), written in the saga voice.

entries.title: The beach of wrecks
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (the first rumours approved: "Sure")
entries.summary: Out west there is a beach lined with wrecked ships that nobody salvages.
entries.heard: fishermen and sailors of the west
lines: There's a beach out west lined with wrecks. Good ships, some of them. Nobody goes to salvage them twice.
Past the far skerries there's a shore where ships just sit and rot. Nobody claims them. Nobody dares.

entries.title: The water that stands up
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (the first rumours approved: "Sure")
entries.summary: Fishermen turn for home before dusk near a certain skerry, because something stands in the water there.
entries.heard: fishermen of the west, and the old fisherman
lines: Don't pass the far skerry at dusk. The water stands up there, and it has faces.
We turn for home before dark out west. Something stands in the water over there, and it watches the boats.

entries.title: The ship with a braid on its prow
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (the first rumours approved: "Sure")
entries.summary: In spring a ship with a woman's braid on its prow comes to the western markets, and its women look the men over.
entries.heard: traders and villagers at the markets of the west, in spring
lines: Every spring a ship with a braid on its prow puts in here. The women on it look at the men like horse-traders.
If a woman off the braided ship asks your name, give it. They say it's an honour. They say a lot of things.

entries.title: Only in summer
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (the first rumours approved: "Sure")
entries.summary: The island takes guests in summer only, and only those it asks.
entries.when: after the hero has heard of the braided ship
lines: The women's island takes guests in summer. Only in summer, and only the ones they ask. Anyone else feeds the sea.
Go with their braid and in their season, or don't go. My cousin tried it in autumn.

entries.title: The thrall ship that never came in
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (the first rumours approved: "Sure")
entries.summary: Long ago a merchant's ship full of women thralls was lost off the western skerries. Some say the women took it.
entries.heard: old traders at the Kaupang, and Old Yngvild
entries.when: after the hero has been a guest on Kvennaey
lines: My grandfather lost a ship out west. Full of women, bound for the east. He swore to his death the women took it.
Before you were born a thrall ship went missing past the skerries. Forty women in collars. Nobody found so much as a plank.

entries.title: No boys on the island
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (the first rumours approved: "Sure")
entries.summary: Those who have been to Kvennaey noticed there were no boys, and learned not to ask.
entries.heard: men who have been guests, the few who came back, and sailors of the west
entries.when: after the hero's first guest season
lines: You were there. Did you see a single boy? No. Don't ask why. Not out loud.
The men they take in summer don't come home. Their ships are the ones on the beach.

entries.title: The sail that the storm went round
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (the first rumours approved: "Sure")
entries.summary: Someone saw Ormr's ship sail calmly through a squall that wrecked others.
lines: I saw his sail go through a squall that put three ships on the rocks. Not a fold in it.
The storm that sank my cousin went round his ship like water round a stone.

entries.title: The one he leaves
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (the first rumours approved: "Sure")
entries.summary: Wherever Ormr burns, he leaves one alive, and on a small island to the west of here it is a smith.
lines: Wherever he burns, he leaves one alive to tell it. On the little island it's a smith, they say. Ask him, if you can stand it.

entries.title: The old man who went into the hill
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (the first rumours approved: "Sure")
entries.summary: An old man in the village went into the troll's hill once, long ago, and came out.
lines: Old Aslak went into the troll's hill when he was young. He came out. His brother didn't. Bring ale if you ask him.

entries.title: The glint in the oaks
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (the first rumours approved: "Sure")
entries.summary: At midsummer dusk something golden is seen in the oak groves, and whoever sees it has a good year.
lines: Go to the oaks at midsummer dusk and look sideways, not straight. Don't tell anyone what you see.

entries.title: The one-eyed guest
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (the first rumours approved: "Sure")
entries.summary: Folk warn that an old one-eyed stranger who asks for your fire should get your best seat.
lines: If an old one-eyed man asks for your fire, give him the best seat. My grandfather didn't, once.
Feed every stranger who comes at dusk. You never know who has been walking a long way.

entries.title: The ring with every rune
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (the first rumours approved: "Sure")
entries.summary: Somewhere there is a ring Odin made himself, with every rune cut in it, and men have drowned looking for it.
entries.heard: skalds, old warriors, anyone in a hall at night
lines: There's a ring Odin forged with his own hands. Every rune there is, cut in it. Men have drowned looking.
Every rune you cut into your ring, he cut first. Into his own. The skalds say it's still out there.

entries.title: The sea that breathes
entries.decided: Robin, 2026-10-17 (the first rumours approved: "Sure")
entries.summary: Out west the sea heaves with no wind, as if something huge were breathing under it.
entries.heard: fishermen of the west, and the old fisherman
lines: Out west the sea goes up and down with no wind on it. My father said it was something breathing.
